gloss: When the sandpiper and clam fight, a third party benefits.
teaser: What happens when two parties are in conflict while an outsider reaps the rewards?
script: Welcome to Chengyu Bites — your quick summary on Chinese 成语. What happens when two parties are in conflict while an outsider reaps the rewards? [break 1s] The phrase is: 鹬蚌相争, yù bàng xiāng zhēng. [break 1s] 鹬 (yù) - sandpiper [break 0.5s] 蚌 (bàng) - clam [break 0.5s] 相 (xiāng) - each other [break 0.5s] 争 (zhēng) - to contend or fight [break 0.5s] The full idiom again: 鹬蚌相争 - literally, 'the sandpiper and clam fight,' and figuratively, it means when two parties are in a conflict, often to the advantage of a third party. [break 1s] Here’s the story behind it: [break 1.5s] In ancient times, a sandpiper and a clam were engaged in a fierce struggle. The sandpiper wanted to eat the clam, while the clam was trying to close its shell to protect itself. Their fight drew the attention of a fisherman, who took advantage of their struggle and caught both. This story illustrates how conflicts can lead to unexpected benefits for outsiders. [break 1.5s] Example one: 两个企业正在鹬蚌相争，第三者却在旁边获利。 [break 1s] Two companies are in a fierce competition, while a third party is profiting on the sidelines. [break 1s] Example two: 在这场辩论中，鹬蚌相争的局面让观众获益。 [break 1s] In this debate, the conflict between two sides benefits the audience. [break 1s] Example three: 他们的争吵只是鹬蚌相争，最后受益的是其他人。 [break 1s] Their argument is just a case of the sandpiper and clam fighting, and the ones who benefit in the end are others. [break 1s] So, remember, 鹬蚌相争 means when two parties are in conflict, and a third party benefits. Thank you for listening to Chengyu Bites! See you next time for another idiom. [break 1s]
